2027-02-28.title: Knanoitho Sunday · The Canaanite Woman
readings: Thus far the Lord has helped us
A house of prayer for all peoples
2027-02-28.alt: Fourth Sunday of the Great Fast. The middle day of the Fast falls on Wednesday 3 March, when the Cross is erected in the church.
2027-02-28.verse: Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.
theo: A Canaanite woman, a foreigner and a pagan, comes shouting after Jesus: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is tormented by a demon.” At first Jesus does not answer her. The disciples want her sent away. Jesus says he was sent to the lost sheep of Israel. But she kneels and says: “Lord, help me.” And when Jesus speaks of the children's bread, she replies: “Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.”

This is one of the most moving prayers in the Gospel. She does not argue about her rights; she does not give up; she accepts being called small, and still trusts. Jesus is amazed: “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.” Her daughter is healed from that hour. Jesus' silence was not a refusal; it was a school of persevering faith.

Isaiah had prophesied that foreigners who hold fast to the covenant would be brought to God's holy mountain, “for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.” The Canaanite mother is the first fruit of that promise. The bread meant for the children is enough for all; in the desert God “rained bread from heaven” for the whole people (Exodus 16:4).

St Paul cries out in Romans: “Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death? Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord!” The mother's cry and Paul's cry are the same: we cannot save ourselves, but Christ can. Halfway through the Fast, the Church sets up the Cross in the middle of the church: the answer to every cry for help.
conn: A house of prayer for all peoples.
Isaiah 56:7, quoted by Jesus when cleansing the Temple, is fulfilled when a Canaanite woman finds mercy.
Crumbs and the bread from heaven.
The manna (Exodus 16) and the multiplication of loaves just before and after this Gospel (Matthew 14–15) point to the Eucharist, offered to all nations.
Samuel's stone “Thus far the LORD has helped us” (1 Samuel 7:12) is the grateful memory of persevering faith.
Sirach 10:12–13: pride begins when we forsake the Lord; the woman's humility opens heaven.
altar: The woman asked only for crumbs from the table. At the Holy Qurbono we receive not crumbs but the whole Bread of Life. Let us come with her humility: “Lord, I am not worthy.”
outline: When God seems silent: do we give up?
Silence, refusal, and still she kneels: “Lord, help me.”
She accepts being small and trusts anyway.
Isaiah 56: God's house is for everyone; welcome the stranger.
Mid-Fast: the Cross set up in our church; renew your Lenten resolutions.
live: Take up again a prayer you abandoned because God seemed silent.
Mothers and fathers: bring each child's needs to Jesus by name, like the Canaanite mother.
Show kindness to someone of another background, language or faith this week.
fathers: Christ delayed the gift not to drive her away but to reveal her faith; her persistence made her an example to all the ages (Homilies on Matthew 52).
He praises the mother whose love for her daughter made her bold, and whose humility drew mercy from the Lord of the table (Commentary on the Diatessaron).
magis: Jesus teaches filial boldness in prayer: “Whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you receive it.” He is amazed at the faith of the Canaanite woman.
Everyone is called to enter the Kingdom; announced first to Israel, it is meant for all nations.
saints: 3 Mar (Wednesday): the middle day of the Great Fast; erection of the Cross (Gogultho). 7 Mar: K'piphtho Sunday. 9 Mar: the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste.
2027-02-28.prayer: Lord Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on us. Give us the humble, persevering faith of the Canaanite mother; hear our prayers for our children and families; and make your Church a house of prayer for all peoples. Amen.

quick: Persevering prayer: when God seems silent, keep asking.
Humble faith wins mercy: “even the dogs eat the crumbs.”
God's house is a house of prayer for all peoples.
2027-02-28.action: Take up again a prayer you stopped because God seemed silent.
2027-02-28.question: Have I given up asking God for something important?
2027-02-28.special: Knanoitho Sunday, fourth Sunday of the Great Fast. Announce the middle day of the Fast (Wednesday 3 March) and the erection of the Cross.
illus: A Kerala mother prayed for twenty years for her son who had left home and faith. Every Sunday she lit a candle before Mary. When he came back one Easter, he said: “I knew someone was praying.” The Canaanite woman still lives in our parishes.

family.explain: A mother whose daughter was very sick kept asking Jesus for help, even when he did not answer at first. Because she kept trusting, Jesus healed her daughter.
family.intention: We pray for all mothers and fathers who are worried about their children.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we need to keep asking Jesus for as a family?”

kidsaint: Kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold as a slave, she later came to know Jesus in Italy, became a sister, and forgave those who had hurt her. Lesson: God's love is for everyone, from every nation.
term: Knanoitho means “the Canaanite woman”. The fourth Sunday of the Great Fast reads the healing of her daughter (Matthew 15:21–28; Mark 7:24–30).
termMore: On the Wednesday after this Sunday, the twenty-fifth day of the Fast, the Malankara Church marks the middle of the Great Fast; the Cross (Gogultho) is solemnly set up in the church, recalling the bronze serpent lifted up in the desert (Numbers 21:9; John 3:14).

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today a mother comes to Jesus. She is not one of his people; she is a Canaanite, a foreigner. Her daughter is suffering terribly. She cries out: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David!” And Jesus does not answer her a word.

Have you ever felt that? You pray and pray, and heaven seems silent. The disciples even want her sent away. Jesus says he was sent first to Israel. But she does not give up. She kneels and says three simple words: “Lord, help me.” And when Jesus speaks of the children's bread, she answers with amazing humility: “Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.”

Jesus is amazed: “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.” His silence was not a refusal. It was a school of faith, and she passed with honours. Isaiah had said that God's house would be a house of prayer for all peoples. This foreign mother shows us that no one is outside God's mercy.

This Wednesday we reach the middle of the Fast, and the Cross is set up in our church. Look at it when you feel God is silent. St Paul cries: “Who will rescue me? Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord!” Mothers and fathers, keep praying for your children. Don't give up. Say with her: “Lord, help me.” Amen.
kids: Children, a mother came to Jesus because her daughter was very sick. She asked and asked: “Jesus, please help!” At first Jesus did not answer.
But she kept trusting and asking. Jesus said: “Your faith is great!” And her daughter was healed.
When you pray and nothing seems to happen, don't stop! Jesus is listening. Let's say: “Jesus, help me!”

intro: A foreign mother cries out for her daughter. Jesus is silent; the disciples want her sent away; she is answered with a hard word. Yet she persists, and Jesus praises her great faith. Her story teaches us how to pray when God seems silent.

sub: She is a Canaanite, an outsider, yet she calls Jesus “Lord, Son of David”.
She brings her daughter's suffering as her own: “Have mercy on me.”
Isaiah's prayer is hers and ours: “O LORD, be gracious to us; we wait for you.”
q: O LORD, be gracious to us; we wait for you. Be our arm every morning, our salvation in the time of trouble.
Just then a Canaanite woman from that region came out and started shouting, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is tormented by a demon.”
points.apply: Pray this week for children in trouble: sick, addicted, lost or far from God.

sub: “He did not answer her at all.” God's silence is not his absence.
The Psalmist also cried: “How long, O LORD?”
She does not leave; she kneels: “Lord, help me.” Persistent, humble prayer grows deeper through testing.
q: How long, O LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
But he did not answer her at all … But she came and knelt before him, saying, “Lord, help me.”
points.apply: Do not stop praying for the intention you have carried longest.

points.h: Great faith and bread for all
sub: She accepts the hard word humbly and turns it into hope: even the dogs eat the crumbs.
Jesus praises her: “Woman, great is your faith!” and her daughter is healed.
Isaiah foresaw it: foreigners gathered into God's house of prayer for all peoples.
q: These I will bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer … for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
She said, “Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.” Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.”
points.apply: Welcome a stranger or someone from another community in your parish or workplace.

concl: The Canaanite woman shows us humble, persistent, confident faith.
Let us keep praying for those we love, and never doubt that the Lord's table has bread for all.
2027-02-28.resolve: Pray a decade of the Rosary each day this week for a child or young person in difficulty.
